entries.1bb3875b9009a76d: This business renovates detached houses, rental housing and other properties. The main companies are Sekisui House Reform Co., Ltd., Sekisui House Support Plus Co., Ltd., the Sekisui House Real Estate Group and the Sekisui House Construction Group. In the fiscal year ended January 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥186,719 million, and revenue including intersegment internal revenue was ¥187,958 million, up 2.2% year on year. Sekisui House Support Plus, which handles after-sales service, began operations in February 2025, and communication with owners has become even closer. The company is strengthening proposals for large-scale renovations tailored to changes in family composition and lifestyle, and for environmentally focused renovations that incorporate insulation work and energy-saving, energy-generating and energy-storing equipment, and in rental housing it is focusing on full renovations, including floor plan changes. Orders for the Renovation Business as a whole were strong. The number of employees is 4,126 (as of January 31, 2026).

entries.21395d178ec9d3b8: On a consolidated basis for the fiscal year ended January 2026, the group consists of Sekisui House, Ltd., 301 consolidated subsidiaries and 36 equity-method affiliates, and conducts business in detached housing, rental and commercial buildings, construction and civil engineering, rental housing management, remodeling, development and international operations.

entries.34529b77adeb3d24: This business designs, builds on contract and sells detached houses, and is the starting point of the company's business. The main companies are Sekisui House, Ltd. and the Sekisui House Construction Group. In the fiscal year ended January 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥478,799 million, and revenue including intersegment internal revenue was ¥478,952 million, down 0.0% year on year, roughly flat. Strategies are set by price range: the company is focusing on sales of mid- to high-grade products, and for its 1st range products it is pursuing the joint construction business “SI Business,” under which it undertakes the foundation and structural frame construction of wooden houses built by partner companies. The detached-housing ZEH ratio for the Net Zero Energy House “Green First Zero” reached a record high of 96% in fiscal 2024 (April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025; excluding contract-built and sold homes in Hokkaido). This business is handled by the same employees who also work in the Rental and Commercial Building Business, and the combined number of employees for the two businesses is 15,686 (as of January 31, 2026).

entries.3b7621c1a738caef: This segment combines three businesses: real estate brokerage and sales, condominium sales, and urban redevelopment of office buildings, hotels and similar properties. In the fiscal year ended January 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥670,240 million, and revenue including intersegment internal revenue was ¥681,989 million, up 17.1% year on year. Revenue increased from the previous year in all three businesses. The number of employees is 2,044 (as of January 31, 2026).

entries.4c84177ed3bc4a70: This business undertakes construction work for commercial buildings and the design and construction of civil engineering works on contract. The main company is the Konoike Group, and Konoike Construction Co., Ltd. is a consolidated subsidiary in which Sekisui House holds 90.7% of the voting rights. In the fiscal year ended January 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥298,344 million, and revenue including intersegment internal revenue was ¥302,293 million, down 7.0% year on year. Orders were strong for large government building projects in the building business and for private-sector projects in the civil engineering business. The number of employees is 2,457 (as of January 31, 2026).

entries.53ab18fdf673531d: This business develops, sells and manages condominiums. The main companies are Sekisui House, Ltd. and Sekisui House GM Partners Co., Ltd. Revenue in the fiscal year ended January 2026 (including intersegment internal revenue) was ¥122,844 million, up 19.9% year on year. The company has narrowed its condominium brand “Grand Maison” to the city centers of Tokyo, Nagoya, Osaka and Fukuoka, and deliveries of properties such as “Grand Maison Musashikosugi no Mori” (Nakahara Ward, Kawasaki City) and “Grand Maison Fukuoka The Central Luxe” (Chuo Ward, Fukuoka City) progressed well.
entries.540fb560b7743397: Revenue for the fiscal year ended January 2026 was ¥4,197,922 million, an increase of ¥139,339 million (3.4%) from ¥4,058,583 million in the previous fiscal year. The reason was higher revenue from the stock-type and development-type businesses in the domestic business. Revenue by business model (including intersegment revenue) was ¥1,346,059 million for contract-type, ¥900,580 million for stock-type, ¥681,989 million for development-type, and ¥1,286,358 million for international.

Holdings, Inc. that did not recur.
entries.60a9b42f70676c81: This business brokers and sells residential land, existing homes, income-producing real estate and other properties. The main companies are Sekisui House, Ltd. and the Sekisui House Real Estate Group. From February 2025, this business, which had been divided among six companies until the previous fiscal year, was consolidated into one company, Sekisui House Real Estate Co., Ltd. Revenue in the fiscal year ended January 2026 (including intersegment internal revenue) was ¥394,509 million, up 10.8% year on year. Sales of real estate held for sale progressed well, centered on residential land.

entries.a5d5d65fe26a2989: The business sells detached houses overseas, develops and sells residential land, and develops condominiums for sale and rental apartment buildings. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended January 2026 was ¥1,286,358 million, the largest among the reportable segments, up 0.6% from ¥1,278,511 million in the previous year. The core is the detached-housing business in the United States; M.D.C. Holdings, Inc., which was made a wholly owned subsidiary in April 2024, has contributed to results from the start of the current fiscal year. It changed its name to SEKISUI HOUSE U.S., Inc. in September 2025, and in January 2026 restructured its US detached-housing subsidiaries, and has begun operating as the substantive holding company for the US detached-housing business. In the US, potential demand for new housing remains strong, but customers continued to take a wait-and-see stance, and demand slowed. Other businesses include community development and rental housing development in the US, and condominium development in Sydney and Brisbane, Australia. In consolidated revenue by region, the United States accounted for ¥1,176,690 million. The number of employees was 3,281 as of January 31, 2026.

entries.b04689bcbfa6758f: This business leases and manages rental housing and other properties. The main company is the Sekisui House Real Estate Group, and since February 2025, Sekisui House Shāmezon PM companies, which specialize in the rental business, have started operations. In the fiscal year ended January 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥707,428 million, making this the second-largest business among the reportable segments. Revenue including intersegment internal revenue was ¥712,621 million, up 3.7% year on year. In addition to continued orders for rental housing “Shāmezon,” the number of units for which the company is entrusted with management has increased, and occupancy rates remain high. It is also advancing digitalization, including enabling move-in and move-out procedures to be handled collectively via an app and blockchain. The number of employees is 2,108 (as of January 31, 2026).

entries.e98641f243c82751: This business designs and builds rental housing and commercial buildings on contract, and sells them. The main companies are Sekisui House, Ltd. and the Sekisui House Construction Group. In the fiscal year ended January 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥558,082 million, and revenue including intersegment internal revenue was ¥564,813 million, up 3.6% year on year. Focusing on convenient areas close to stations within urban areas, the company is expanding “Shāmezon” rental housing, three- and four-story buildings built with its proprietary construction method. For the net zero energy rental housing “Shāmezon ZEH,” ZEH units accounted for 77% of rental housing orders. Orders for its CRE and PRE business, which proposes the use of real estate held by companies and public bodies, have also been strong, and the company is strengthening proposals for non-residential properties such as offices. This business is handled by the same employees who also work in the Detached Housing Business, and the combined number of employees for the two businesses is 15,686 (as of January 31, 2026).

entries.ece3dcf8e89a6a1f: This is a business segment not included in the reportable segments, engaged in real estate management, non-life insurance agency and other businesses. It also includes the building materials supply business. In the fiscal year ended January 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥6,215 million, and revenue including intersegment internal revenue was ¥16,451 million, up 17.0% year on year. Internal revenue is large relative to revenue from external customers, making this a category with a high share of work within the group. The number of employees is 275 (as of January 31, 2026).
entries.f24710755cabfccd: This business develops, manages and operates office buildings, hotels, rental apartments and other properties. The main companies are Sekisui House, Ltd., Sekisui House Asset Management Co., Ltd. and Sekisui House Hotel Management Co., Ltd. Revenue in the fiscal year ended January 2026 (including intersegment internal revenue) was ¥164,634 million, up 32.7% year on year. The company has narrowed its operating areas to the city centers of Tokyo, Nagoya, Osaka and Fukuoka, and sales of multiple properties, including equity interests in large properties, progressed beyond plan. Occupancy rates for properties the company continues to hold, such as “Prime Maison,” remained firm.
